title: Claude Code 2026: Dynamic Workflows, Agent View & Key Updates
content:
## Overview

The first half of 2026 brought the most significant expansion to Claude Code since its launch. Major capabilities include dynamic workflows for orchestrating hundreds of parallel subagents, a new agent view for managing concurrent sessions, doubled rate limits, and an integrated security-guidance plugin. This page covers the headline updates; see [Claude Code Overview](claude-code-overview) for the foundational concepts.

---

## Dynamic Workflows

Dynamic workflows allow Claude Code to orchestrate **hundreds of parallel subagents from a single session**. In practice, this means:

- A coordinator Claude instance can spawn dozens of specialist agents, assign each a subtask, collect results, and synthesize a final output — all within one user-initiated task.
- Subagents share a filesystem, so one agent can produce a file that another agent reads and processes without any manual file passing.
- Each subagent can have its own model, system prompt, tool configuration, and MCP server connections.

This enables ambitious tasks like "port this 200-file Python codebase to TypeScript" or "audit every API endpoint for security vulnerabilities" to complete in a single Claude Code session with wall-clock times measured in minutes rather than hours.

```json
// Example agent definition for a subagent
{
  "name": "security-auditor",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
  "system": "You are a security auditor. Review the file at the given path for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities and write findings to findings/[filename].md.",
  "tools": ["Read", "Write"]
}
```

---

## Agent View

Agent view is a new CLI interface for managing multiple concurrent Claude Code sessions from a single terminal:

- **Start agents:** Launch multiple sessions (each working on a different branch or subtask) from one view.
- **Background sessions:** Send agents to the background so they continue working while you focus elsewhere.
- **Status at a glance:** See each agent's current status and last response without fully entering the session.
- **Jump back in:** Switch into any session for input when the agent needs clarification.

This replaces the previous pattern of opening multiple terminal tabs for parallel work — everything is managed from one pane.

---

## Rate Limit Increases

Anthropic **doubled rate limits** for Claude Code in early 2026. Specifically:
- API limits for Claude Opus were raised substantially for developer, startup, and enterprise tiers.
- Claude Code's own session limits were doubled, allowing more tool calls per session before hitting throttles.

This directly enables the dynamic workflows feature — orchestrating 100+ subagents requires headroom that previous limits didn't provide.

---

## Security-Guidance Plugin

A new built-in security-guidance plugin proactively reviews Claude's code modifications for vulnerabilities in real-time:

- Scans edits as they happen, flagging potential OWASP Top 10 issues before code is written to disk.
- Integrates with the existing permission model — can be configured to block writes for high-severity findings.
- Works alongside the `/code-review` slash command (which does a post-hoc diff review) as a live guardrail.

---

## `/usage` Visibility

Users can now run `/usage` to see a breakdown of what's consuming plan limits:
- Which skills are running
- Which subagents are active
- Which MCP servers are connected

This helps debug unexpected rate-limit hits and understand the cost profile of complex agentic sessions.

---

## Gateway Model Picker

When `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points to an Anthropic-compatible gateway, the model picker now fetches available models from the gateway's `/v1/models` endpoint rather than showing only Anthropic-hosted models. This makes it easier to use Claude Code against self-hosted or proxy deployments that expose additional models.

---

## Opus 4.8 as Default

Following the release of Claude Opus 4.8 on May 28, 2026, it became the **default model for Max, Team Premium, Enterprise, and API accounts** in Claude Code. It is configured for high effort by default, with an option to dial to even higher intensity for particularly complex tasks. Auto mode on the Pro plan now supports Sonnet 4.6 alongside Opus.
